Variants.Content: Farming and livestock east of the upper Rhine connect through crossings with Roman coins, objects and markets. Closed borders hurt both elite gifts and household exchange; harvest and herds outlast one haul of prizes.

Upper Rhine farming and herding connect through crossings with Roman markets. Traveling followers need real food from this production; valuables still require a buyer and exchange. Closed borders harm Alamannic exchange and chiefly gifts.

Closed borders harm Alamannic exchange and chiefly gifts. Collectors and distributors depend on the next yield too; extra demands leave losses with continuing suppliers. Upper Rhine farming and herding connect through crossings with Roman markets.
